analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials T+1 ... also FIX UNP FAST (5 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Desk says markets were meaningfully higher on 11/4 with volatility collapsing, but rotations under the surface were as violent as the desk has seen. The desk leans toward the move continuing, since nothing changes in the next few months until congressional seats turn over.

The desk names a swifter resolution of the geopolitical situation as the other catalyst. It would lead to lower rates, lower inflationary pressure and more of the prior day's price action. The catalyst path looks murky into year end while investors have degrossed and sit on the sidelines.
Pre-market on 11/5: US futures little changed with technology shares continuing to sell off. KOSPI is down 528bps, Japan down 179bps, SHPROP up 156bps and Europe up 50bps at the index level.
Eurozone September PPI came in at +11.1% vs +10.6% consensus. German factory orders rebounded in September in line with expectations.
WTI remains below $90 and Brent is at $96. The US 10-year yield is 4.88%, at local lows on growth concerns. Bitcoin is just above $80k and the dollar is flat.
Chart flag: the industrials momentum pair (GSINMOMO) had its second worst day on record (since 2013).

FAST daily sales rose +17.1% vs ~15% expected, outperforming the benchmark by ~170bps. Heavy manufacturing led at +23%, with cutting tools and abrasives leading by usage. 71% of the top 100 national accounts are growing and headcount is up 1%, which the desk says should help operating leverage.

FIX increased its share repurchase program by 1mm shares (~$1bn). The STB denied UNP's appeal and UNP is to submit additional documents. MGA renewed its normal course issuer bid for up to 25.8mm shares.
PH and CMI are the focus among the remaining reports to come on 11/5.

Pre-market prints: APD Q4 EPS $3.61 roughly in line on a topline beat, with fiscal 2027 guide of $14.15-15.40 vs $14.45 consensus. Q1 EPS guide midpoint is below consensus. Americas beat on revenue and EBIT while Asia and Europe were weak, with overall margins well below.
ROK Q4 EPS $3.88 beat $3.69 on sales below consensus ($2.33bn vs $2.41bn). FY27 EPS guide $14.50-15.50 has a midpoint just above $14.90 consensus.
VNT Q3 EPS $0.92 vs $0.84 and EBITDA $179mm vs $163mm. Raised FY EPS guide to $3.60-3.64 vs $3.49 consensus.
AAP cut the low end of its FY EPS guide and sees sales at the low end of its range, with comps +1%. WMS missed on sales ($889mm vs $932mm) and trimmed its full-year topline guide.

Overnight prints with raised guidance: ITT (EPS $2.26 vs $2.08, FY EPS $8.54-8.62 vs $8.12-8.32 prior), TPC (EPS $1.83 vs $0.80, guide $5.90-6.10 vs $5.15-5.45 prior), CW, VSEC, WTS, MATX and OEC. Misses and cuts: TTAM (EPS $0.22 vs $0.37, EBITDA margin to decline 250-300bps), NTR (EPS $0.61 vs $0.79, FY EBITDA cut), TROX (Q4 EBITDA guide $80-90mm vs $92mm consensus) and AMRC (transition period EPS outlook lowered).
